### Walkthrough `AddAppStoreApp` now checks the shared-token rule for additional Apple-platform versions before version-name and version-count validation. If the request omits a token, the method reuses the existing token. If the request specifies a different token, the method returns a conflict. Tests cover unnamed and named versions with conflicting tokens, and a duplicate version name with a matching token. **Possibly related PRs** - [fleetdm/fleet#56034](https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/pull/56034): Adds the shared-token behavior that this change checks earlier in `AddAppStoreApp`. - [fleetdm/fleet#56640](https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/pull/56640): Includes the Apple app-add flow whose token-conflict validation order this change updates. **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium
Merge Risk: Low · up to aa5ea

Token conflicts now take precedence as requested. A concurrent deletion can produce an unexpected 404 during an add; this bounded edge case warrants owner awareness but does not materially block merging.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: the VPP token conflict check now runs before the version-name and version-limit checks when adding App Store apps. It uses the conventional fix: prefix, and it matches the linked issue `#58055` and the code changes in ee/server/service/vpp.go and vpp_test.go. The title is 62 characters, which is within a normal length.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template. It links the issue (Fixes `#58055` and Resolves `#58055`), explains the root cause and the fix, and includes the testing section. It also includes the required AI section in the format '**AI:** <tool> (<model ID>)'. It lists the changes file exception, but it does not check the QA box. It has no frontend screenshots, but that does not apply to this backend change. The database, MDM, GitOps, and fleetd sections are not filled in, which is expected because they do not apply. The description omits the required changes file line, which is justified as an exception. The AI model is recorded as 'unknown', which the template allows when the model ID is not known.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#58055` requires that adding an App Store app already added to the fleet for the same platform from another VPP token return the token-conflict message, whether or not `name` is set. The diff of ee/server/service/vpp.go moves the existing-token block in AddAppStoreApp from after the version-limit check to a position after the existing version count is loaded and before the versionNameExists check. For an Apple platform with an existing version, the block returns fleet.ConflictError with 'Couldn't add software. %s (%s) is already added to this fleet from the %q VPP token.' when the requested token differs. When the token is omitted, the existing token is reused. Because the token check now runs first, an omitted name no longer reaches the 'Default version' conflict for a different token. The same-token duplicate-name path still returns the existing 'A version named ...' conflict. The test diff in ee/server/service/vpp_test.go covers the cross-token conflict with name='' and name='US copy', and the same-token duplicate default-name conflict. I did not execute the tests. The conclusion rests on the diff and the test assertions.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The production change is a single reordering of an existing block in AddAppStoreApp. It adds no new behavior beyond the issue's requirement, and it adds no new dependencies or declarations. The moved block uses only variables already in scope (appID, teamID, existingVersionCount, versionNameExists) and the existing datastore and error helpers. The test changes are limited to TestAddAppStoreAppToken. They cover the cross-token conflict for the omitted-name and custom-name cases and the same-token duplicate-name case, all tied to `#58055`. No unrelated files are changed in the reviewed diff. Side effect: when the token differs and the version limit is also reached, the token conflict now takes precedence. This follows from the issue's ordering requirement and is not unrelated work.
